prediction_cards.expected_observation: The first crossing rank stabilizes under dualization and is invariant under adding join-irrelevant elements below rank k.
prediction_cards.gate: If a rank-1 crossing witness cannot be delayed by any join-sealed filtration, the mother-structure claim is too coarse.
prediction_cards.horizon: 3 finite lattice families or 2 weeks of proof-search traces, whichever comes first.
prediction_cards.intervention: Restrict the proof search to k-generated ideals and compare the first failure rank across joins and order duals.
prediction_cards.measurement: For each finite test lattice, compute the smallest rank where a crossing pair appears after all monotone joins over generated ideals up to size k.
prediction_cards.novelty_reason: Local monotone-join facts alone do not force a rank-stability claim for first failure across dualization.
prediction_cards.prediction: There exists a minimal filtration index k such that all uncrossedness failures appear first at rank k+1 and never earlier, when joins are taken over k-generated priority ideals.
prediction_cards.receipt: One explicit counterexample lattice with the witness pair, join table, and rank annotation.
prediction_cards.refuter: A finite priority-lattice example where uncrossedness fails at rank 1 but is repaired only by a non-join operation.

prediction_cards.expected_observation: Exactly one local join-absorption pattern blocks all crossings; modularity without that pattern does not.
prediction_cards.gate: If the proposed separator does not isolate one join-absorption pattern, the correspondence collapses.
prediction_cards.horizon: 5 proof branches or 1 week of automated lemma search.
prediction_cards.intervention: Swap the absorption axiom in the candidate proof skeleton and record whether the crossing witness can still be eliminated.
prediction_cards.measurement: Check whether uncrossedness survives after replacing one join-absorption step with its weaker modular analogue.
prediction_cards.novelty_reason: Neither side’s local theory alone forces a single-axiom separator between modular and distributive behavior.
prediction_cards.prediction: A minimal axiom set for uncrossedness will separate distributive from modular hypotheses by one specific join-absorption test rather than by the usual global lattice law.
prediction_cards.receipt: Two lattices, one modular-non-distributive and one distributive, with identical separator outputs but different crossing outcomes.
prediction_cards.refuter: A modular non-distributive finite lattice where the candidate separator does not distinguish crossing behavior from the distributive case.

prediction_cards.expected_observation: Templates split into at least two strata with distinct first-failure join-depths, and the same split mirrors the left-side rank threshold.
prediction_cards.gate: If strength edges do not produce distinct first-failure strata, the template family is not separated enough.
prediction_cards.intervention: Generate finite countermodels while increasing only the join-depth bound, holding all other template clauses fixed.
prediction_cards.measurement: For each template, record the smallest finite model size and join-depth that falsifies it.
prediction_cards.novelty_reason: A standard finite-model stress test does not by itself predict a shared rank threshold with priority-join uncrossedness.
prediction_cards.prediction: For a named axiom template family, countermodels will stratify by the least join-depth at which the template fails, and that depth will match the left-side crossing rank.
prediction_cards.receipt: A model certificate with template labels, failed clauses, and minimality witness.
prediction_cards.refuter: A finite countermodel that falsifies two supposedly adjacent axiom templates at the same minimal size and depth.

prediction_cards.expected_observation: At least one diamond edge pattern remains stable under clause perturbation and corresponds to a left-side distributive-vs-modular separator.
prediction_cards.gate: If the strength graph collapses to a single obstruction type, the diamond separator prediction fails.
prediction_cards.intervention: Perturb one template clause at a time and re-run finite countermodel search to see whether the diamond persists.
prediction_cards.measurement: Construct the implication graph of templates and note the smallest countermodel for each edge.
prediction_cards.novelty_reason: Local model checking alone does not force a diamond strength geometry linked to an uncrossedness separator.
prediction_cards.prediction: Strength edges between axiom templates will form a non-chain with one diamond-shaped separator: two incomparable weakenings fail in different countermodel strata but share the same kill condition at the next stronger template.
prediction_cards.receipt: A perturbation log showing identical failure witnesses across all tested template variants.
prediction_cards.refuter: A countermodel search where every perturbation of the template family yields the same kill condition.

prediction_cards.expected_observation: The operator is needed exactly where order duality otherwise breaks the argument.
prediction_cards.gate: If duality changes the threshold value, the shared closure schema is wrong.
prediction_cards.horizon: 2 proof-search iterations or 1 day of symbolic rewriting.
prediction_cards.intervention: Introduce a synthetic closure operator and test whether the crossing elimination step depends on it.
prediction_cards.measurement: Inspect whether the proof search can be rewritten with an explicit closure operator satisfying idempotence on generated cones.
prediction_cards.novelty_reason: The local lattice facts do not force the appearance of a duality-stable closure operator.
prediction_cards.prediction: Any proof of uncrossedness that survives order duality must factor through a closure operator that is idempotent on join-generated priority cones.
prediction_cards.receipt: Paired primal and dual examples with threshold comparison and witness traces.
prediction_cards.refuter: A dualized finite example where the uncrossedness threshold changes without any change in the join-generated filtration.

prediction_cards.expected_observation: The threshold index is unchanged, while the witness orientation reverses.
prediction_cards.gate: If the argument cannot be localized to an idempotent closure, the schema is too rigid.
prediction_cards.intervention: Dualize the order while keeping the join-based filtration fixed.
prediction_cards.measurement: Run the same finite test suite on the dual order and compare the first threshold where crossings appear or disappear.
prediction_cards.novelty_reason: A dual-stable threshold is not implied by either side’s local theory alone.
prediction_cards.prediction: If one swaps to the order dual, the same minimal axioms will still determine the uncrossedness threshold, but with the closure direction reversed and no change in the threshold value.
prediction_cards.receipt: A local proof audit marking the non-idempotent step and its dependency chain.
prediction_cards.refuter: A proof fragment showing uncrossedness depends on a non-closure, non-idempotent step that cannot be localized.

prediction_cards.expected_observation: At least one subclass has exact dual obstruction symmetry and one does not.
prediction_cards.gate: If syntax changes alter the strength graph, the closure schema lacks invariance.
prediction_cards.intervention: Generate the dual countermodel and compare its obstruction signature to the original.
prediction_cards.measurement: For each finite template, check whether the smallest countermodel survives dualization as the same obstruction type.
prediction_cards.novelty_reason: Finite-model stress alone does not predict a closure-preserving symmetry classification.
prediction_cards.prediction: Template families will split into closure-preserving and non-closure-preserving subclasses, and only the former will admit symmetric dual countermodels.
prediction_cards.receipt: Two equivalent encodings with different first-failure clauses and countermodel certificates.
prediction_cards.refuter: A template family whose minimal countermodel changes obstruction type under mere re-encoding.

prediction_cards.expected_observation: The edge direction and first-failure clause remain unchanged under re-encoding.
prediction_cards.gate: If self-duality does not correlate with closure preservation, the correspondence fails.
prediction_cards.intervention: Use two equivalent presentations and ask whether the first-failure clause remains the same.
prediction_cards.measurement: Re-encode the same axiom template in two syntactically different forms and compare the resulting strength graph.
prediction_cards.novelty_reason: Presentation invariance of strength edges is a new constraint not forced by ordinary model search.
prediction_cards.prediction: The first failed closure clause will determine a canonical strength edge direction that is invariant under swapping the presentation of axioms.
prediction_cards.receipt: A self-dual model certificate plus a report of the violated closure clause.
prediction_cards.refuter: A family in which every countermodel is self-dual but the axiom templates are not closure-preserving.

prediction_cards.expected_observation: At least two incomparable minimal separator sets occur.
prediction_cards.gate: If minimal separators collapse to one universal fact, the hypergraph claim is overfit.
prediction_cards.intervention: Search over finite lattices for minimal separator sets under varying priority preorders.
prediction_cards.measurement: Enumerate all minimal join fact sets that eliminate crossings and test whether any contains another.
prediction_cards.novelty_reason: The local theory may show separability, but not antichain structure of minimal separators.
prediction_cards.prediction: The minimal set of join facts needed to prevent crossings forms a hyperedge antichain, not a chain, even in finite distributive cases.
prediction_cards.receipt: A complete join-fact enumeration with the unique universal separator marked.
prediction_cards.refuter: A finite lattice where a single join fact always suffices to block all crossings, so no antichain separator exists.

prediction_cards.expected_observation: Orientation changes witness minimality without changing the underlying separator hyperedge.
prediction_cards.gate: If dual witnesses do not share the same separator support, the correspondence fails.
prediction_cards.intervention: Compute witness families in both orientations and compare their minimal supports.
prediction_cards.measurement: Count minimal crossing witnesses before and after dualization and check whether they collapse to the same separator hyperedge.
prediction_cards.novelty_reason: This cross-orientation separator reuse is not forced by the local join arguments.
prediction_cards.prediction: A single separator hyperedge will correspond to a family of order-dual witnesses, and each witness will be minimal only in one orientation.
prediction_cards.receipt: Primal/dual witness sets with support signatures and mismatch annotation.
prediction_cards.refuter: An orientation pair with different underlying separator hyperedges.

prediction_cards.expected_observation: At least one non-nested minimal cut pair survives all small clause perturbations.
prediction_cards.gate: If every minimal countermodel cut is nested, the separator hypergraph is too weak.
prediction_cards.intervention: Add or remove one clause from a template and recompute the cut poset.
prediction_cards.measurement: Build the cut poset from countermodels and check whether the minimal cuts form an antichain.
prediction_cards.novelty_reason: Finite-model stress typically reports failures, not cut-antichain geometry.
prediction_cards.prediction: Axiom templates will produce a separator hypergraph whose minimal cuts are not nested; the nesting failure will identify the weakest viable template family.
prediction_cards.receipt: A cut-poset certificate showing chain structure across all tested templates.
prediction_cards.refuter: A template family whose cut poset is always a chain.

prediction_cards.expected_observation: Robust edges are exactly those with strict separator containment.
prediction_cards.gate: If implication is not tracked by strict support containment, the mother structure does not explain the edge.
prediction_cards.intervention: Perturb one axiom clause and test whether support containment remains strict.
prediction_cards.measurement: For each robust implication edge, compare the underlying minimal countermodel supports.
prediction_cards.novelty_reason: Logical implication and separator containment need not coincide absent the shared mother structure.
prediction_cards.prediction: Every strength edge that survives perturbation will correspond to strict containment of separator hyperedges, not merely to logical implication.
prediction_cards.receipt: Two template certificates with identical supports but different implication status.
prediction_cards.refuter: An implication edge that holds despite equal separator supports on both sides.
